lines.trans: The young woman called yesterday about the hostess vacancy.
She was told to come see us this evening.
Nastya, your mom just called over there.
She said that the little boy's fever went up.
Then tell Vika that I left urgently.
Kostya, have you heard the main news of the day yet?
It seems the hotel owner Eleonora is sleeping with Max!
Come on, where did you get such nonsense from?
I saw him near her suite with my own eyes!
He was just quietly walking out of her room.
She invited him tonight to get whatever he wants!
Then soon we are going to have a new head chef!

examples.trans: After all, the main thing for you is that I dump your daughter.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Я собственными глазами видел его возле номера!
examples.trans: I saw him near her suite with my own eyes!

examples.text: Я собственными глазами это видел!
examples.trans: I saw it with my own eyes!

examples.text: Я вижу машинку.
examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я прекрасно понимаю, как важен этот матч.
examples.trans: I understand perfectly how important this match is.

examples.text: Правда, потом она себе их и забрала.
examples.trans: True, later she took them back for herself.

examples.text: Он мне бутылку виски уже полгода отдаёт.
examples.trans: He has been owing me a bottle of whiskey for half a year.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'near', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он в банке работает на перевозке денег.
examples.trans: He works at the bank transporting money.

examples.text: Шеф, да эту модель просто невозможно собрать!
examples.trans: Chef, it is simply impossible to assemble this model!

examples.text: Она уже паркуется возле нашего служебного входа.
examples.trans: She is already parking near our service entrance.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Держи ключ, можешь принять душ в моём номере.
examples.trans: Take the key, you can take a shower in my hotel room.

examples.text: Можешь принять душ в моём номере.
examples.trans: You can take a shower in my room.

examples.text: Но в современном центре персонал гораздо получше.
examples.trans: But at a modern center the staff is much better.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как тебе это удалось? Их нет в продаже!
examples.trans: How did you manage that? They are sold out!

examples.text: Я прекрасно понимаю, как важен этот матч.
examples.trans: I understand perfectly how important this match is.

examples.text: А как же мне тогда достать рюмку?
examples.trans: Then how am I supposed to get the shot glass?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет, это наш с тобой общий праздник.
examples.trans: No, this is our shared holiday together.

examples.text: Мы же хотели отпраздновать этот день вместе.
examples.trans: We wanted to celebrate this day together.

examples.text: А праздник мы отметим в другой день.
examples.trans: And we will celebrate the holiday on another day.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Лёва, быстро спрячься, сиди там тихо!
examples.trans: Lyova, hide quickly, sit quietly in there!

examples.text: Он как раз тихо выходил из её номера.
examples.trans: He was just quietly walking out of her room.

examples.text: Тише, дети спят!
examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'walked out, left', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.text: Он как раз тихо выходил из её номера.
examples.trans: He was just quietly walking out of her room.

examples.text: Я выхожу через минуту.
examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это мне вчера знакомый из банка принёс.
examples.trans: An acquaintance from the bank brought me this yesterday.

examples.text: Да, она внизу, ей что-нибудь нужно передать?
examples.trans: Yes, she is downstairs, should I pass anything on to her?

examples.text: Тогда я пойду обратно вниз на работу.
examples.trans: Then I will go back downstairs to work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calls, summons', paired with 'звать'.

examples.text: Она позвала его вечером получить всё что хочет!
examples.trans: She invited him tonight to get whatever he wants!

examples.text: Дядя Аркадий всё починит и позовёт.
examples.trans: Uncle Arkady will fix everything and call you.

examples.text: Позвать врача.
examples.trans: To call a doctor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: Считаю до трёх, кто останется — получит штраф!
examples.trans: I am counting to three, whoever stays will get fined!

examples.text: Там и получишь всё то, что хочешь.
examples.trans: There you will get everything that you want.

examples.text: Она позвала его вечером получить всё что хочет!
examples.trans: She invited him tonight to get whatever he wants!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Уходите, я сам тут всё спокойно доделаю!
examples.trans: Go, I will calmly finish everything here myself!

examples.text: А вам разве не всё равно, сколько платить?
examples.trans: Do you not care how much you pay?

examples.text: Посмотри, какой же ты всё-таки нетерпеливый парень!
examples.trans: Look what an impatient guy you are after all!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wants', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Мы же хотели отпраздновать этот день вместе.
examples.trans: We wanted to celebrate this day together.

examples.text: Если она не занята, я хотела бы поработать.
examples.trans: If it is not taken, I would like to work here.

examples.text: Доченька, я просто хотела, чтобы ты была счастлива!
examples.trans: Sweetheart, I just wanted you to be happy!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А теперь у них скоро родится ребёнок.
examples.trans: And now they are going to have a baby soon.

examples.text: Шикарно, скажите, сколько я вам за него должен?
examples.trans: Splendid, tell me, how much do I owe you for it?

examples.text: Привет, Витя, мы скоро едем на стадион?
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, are we heading to the stadium soon?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Почему же я должен быть таким добрым?
examples.trans: Why then should I be so kind to you?

examples.text: Почему я должен быть добрым?
examples.trans: Why should I be kind?

examples.text: Может быть, ты имеешь в виду Фридмана?
examples.trans: Perhaps you mean Friedman?
